newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins ease in quiet trade on US holiday.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins ease in quiet trade on US holiday.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds eased on Monday and dealers said the market was pausing for breath as the U.S. Columbus Day holiday was subduing activity.

"Many London and Russian operators are no longer trading because of this holiday," Moscow Business World Bank dealer Sergei Kolzharov said. Prices had firmed in early trading on short-covering, he said.
But Inkombank dealer Alexander Nikolayev said prices had edged down recently on low-volume local selling.
Despite today's dip in thin trading, dealers saw prices of the most liquid third, fourth and fifth MinFins higher ahead of the issue of Russia's first Eurobond expected this year.
Kolzharov said fluctuations would be likely in the ranges of 58.00-60.50, 41.00-44.00 and 81.50-84.00 respectively.
Nikolayev forecast the fourth and fifth tranches could rise at maximum as high as 64.00 and 46.00 respectively.
He added the shortest maturity was unlikely to rise much from the current level as it yielded some 11 percent, with the Eurobond's expected yield around 10 percent.
